items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: Clapton has, there’s a great thing on Clapton, it’s called Life in Twelve Bars.

ctx.x: And I don’t know if it’s just because it’s too much a technical musical thing, but I don’t think the 12-bar blues gets the recognition it should as this incredible, precise musical form that can be used in so many different ways.

Well I obviously began my life, my career, playing basically 12-bar blues, whether it was rhythm & blues, blues, soul music in the early days, rhythm & blues/soul music, country. And basically, you’re talking about 12-bar manuscripts. Clapton has, there’s a great thing on Clapton, it’s called Life in Twelve Bars. And that sums it up, doesn’t it? Now of course things got way more sophisticated. But that’s, to me — I’m not the guy who said oh that’s what it was, it was all based on 12-bar blues. I’m not the first…
Yes I do. And that’s sort of why I wanted your opinion on it. It’s so elastic. It’s like a chameleon almost you know.
